title: Junkman Rag, 'Shots and Shells' and a Civil War song
summary: Allen asks about Junkman Rag, which Nash needs to practice; Nash sings part of 'Shots and Shells'/battlefield song, and does not know 'Just Before the Battle, Mother'.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Let's see. What else do we have now? That's what I remember. Do you remember much of Junkman Rag enough to play it on the yuk or you got to practice up on that?
Sure I had to practice up on that I reckon, yes.
Okay. Do you remember shots and shells or ringing on the battlefield?
I believe I can get some of that. I wouldn't say I know all of that but yeah.
Well, it's better to give it a try than not to do it at all, you know. So let's try it then. I'm sorry. I'm sorry.

I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I want to get to build this bamboo Boys, our flag is done. Just bring the news to mother and tell her how did I love her And kiss how did sweet live for me For I'm not coming home Just saying that is no other Can take the place of mother And kiss how did sweet live for me For I'm not coming home That's all I can remember. That's a whole, whole number. That's a pretty one. Boy, that killed on the battlefield.
Do you remember that old Civil War song, Just Before the Battle Your Mother?
Just before, no. Just Before the Battle Mother? No, I ain't got that.
